proposals: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should notify the 1%, 2% and 5% SAF blending targets for 2027, 2028 and 2030 as a binding schedule stating which routes they cover, so that the mandate driving this post’s hydrogen arithmetic is no longer only indicative.

MoPNG should publish a national SAF roadmap allocating expected 2030 volumes by pathway — HEFA, ATJ, PtL, PBtL — with the green hydrogen each implies, since the difference between roughly 40 and 528 kilotonnes a year depends entirely on that mix.

Indian Oil Corporation should publish the feedstock, technology licensor, capacity and commissioning date of each SAF unit at Panipat as separate entries, so that the conflicting reports of one plant running both used cooking oil and LanzaJet’s alcohol-to-jet technology can be resolved.

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy should track SAF as a named demand segment under the National Green Hydrogen Mission and report its projected hydrogen draw each year, so that the link between the SAF mandate and the hydrogen cost curve is monitored as one policy, not two.
